'''Houston Alexander Gaines''' (born January 11, 1995) is an American politician from Georgia. Gaines has been a [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] member of the [[Georgia House of Representatives]] since 2019.

In July 2025, he became the first prominent Republican to enter the race for the open [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]] seat in [[Georgia's 10th congressional district]] currently represented by Republican [[Mike Collins (politician)|Mike Collins]], who is the Republican nominee in the [[2026 United States Senate election in Georgia|2026 U.S. Senate election in Georgia]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bluestein |first1=Greg |title=Athens lawmaker launches U.S. House bid for open GOP-leaning Georgia seat |work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |url=https://www.ajc.com/politics/2025/07/athens-lawmaker-launches-us-house-bid-for-open-gop-leaning-georgia-seat/ |access-date=22 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Raymond |first1=Jonathan |title=Republican state representative announces run for congressional seat being vacated by Collins |date=31 July 2025 |url=https://www.11alive.com/article/news/politics/state-rep-houston-gaines-campaign-for-congress-georgia-10th-district/85-217e9f17-60f4-4c17-96d0-80361415755f |publisher=11Alive |access-date=22 August 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Bluestein |first1=Greg |title=Collins kicks off U.S. Senate bid in Georgia with show of force |work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |url=https://www.ajc.com/politics/2025/08/collins-kicks-off-us-senate-bid-in-georgia-with-show-of-force/ |access-date=22 August 2025}}</ref>

In April 2026, President [[Donald Trump]] and [[speaker of the United States House of Representatives|U.S. Speaker of the House]] [[Mike Johnson]] endorsed Gaines in the Republican primary for Georgia's 10th congressional district.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mitchell |first1=Tia |title=Trump endorses Republican front-runners in Georgia races for U.S. House |work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |url=https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/04/trump-endorses-republican-front-runners-in-georgia-races-for-us-house/ |access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Verity |first1=Kate |title=Donald Trump endorses Houston Gaines in race for District 10 seat |work=The Covington News |url=https://www.covnews.com/news/state/donald-trump-endorses-houston-gaines-in-race-for-district-10-seat/ |access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref>

==Early life==
On January 11, 1995, Gaines was born in [[Athens, Georgia]]. Gaines' grandfather is the late Judge Joseph Gaines.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ourcampaigns.com/CandidateDetail.html?CandidateID=392594 |title=Gaines, Houston |website=ourcampaigns.com |accessdate=April 15, 2021}}</ref><ref name="votesmart_gaines"/>

==Education==
In 2017, Gaines earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Political Science and Economics from [[University of Georgia]]'s [[University of Georgia School of Public and International Affairs]] and [[University of Georgia]]'s [[Terry College of Business]]. In 2016, Gaines served as the Student Government Association president, until 2017.<ref name="redandblack_gaines2019"/><ref name="votesmart_gaines"/>  During his time at school, he also served as the campaign manager for Athens Mayor [[Nancy Denson]]'s ultimately successful campaign.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mayor Denson: Age Is Just A Number |url=https://gradynewsource.uga.edu/mayor-denson-age-is-just-a-number/ |website=Grady NewSource |publisher=University of Georgia |access-date=21 September 2025}}</ref>  As Mayor, Denson would later throw a fundraiser for Gaines's Republican State House campaign in 2017 and be subsequently removed from the local Democratic Party Committee.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lefevre |first1=Kaley |title=BREAKING: Athens-Clarke County Democratic Committee votes to remove Mayor Nancy Denson from committee |url=https://www.redandblack.com/athensnews/breaking-athens-clarke-county-democratic-committee-votes-to-remove-mayor-nancy-denson-from-committee/article_4e614594-a4ac-11e7-825a-738d1f33ad1b.html |website=Red & Black |access-date=21 September 2025}}</ref>

==Career==
[[File:Houston Gaines 2024.png|thumb|Gaines at a [[University of Georgia]] College Republicans event, 2024.|upright]]
In 2017, at age 22, Gaines ran in a special election for the [[Georgia House of Representatives]] and was defeated by Democrat [[Deborah Gonzalez]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Houston Gaines |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Houston_Gaines}}</ref> On November 6, 2018, Gaines defeated Gonzalez in a rematch of their 2017 race and became a Republican member of the [[Georgia House of Representatives]] for District 117, winning with 53.55% of the votes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=841131 |title=GA State House 117 |website=ourcampaigns.com |date=November 6, 2018 |accessdate=April 15, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.redandblack.com/athensnews/breaking-houston-gaines-takes-back-state-house-district-117-clarke-county-finishes-reporting/article_bc0ee874-e242-11e8-a40e-23d9972c450c.html |title=BREAKING: Houston Gaines takes back state House District 117, Clarke County finishes reporting |publisher=Redandblack.com |date=2018-11-06 |access-date=2020-12-22}}</ref> On November 3, 2020, as an incumbent, Gaines won the election and continued serving [[Georgia's 117th House of Representatives district|District 117]]. Gaines defeated Mokah Jasmine Johnson with 56.58% of the votes.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=895399 |title=GA State House 117 |website=ourcampaigns.com |date=November 3, 2020 |accessdate=April 15, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.legis.ga.gov/members/house/4955?session=27 |title=Representative Houston Gaines |publisher=Legis.ga.gov |access-date=2020-12-22}}</ref><ref name="votesmart_gaines">{{cite web |url=https://justfacts.votesmart.org/candidate/biography/176757/houston-gaines |title=Houston Gaines' Biography |publisher=[[Vote Smart]] |accessdate=April 14, 2021}}</ref>

In the [[2022 Georgia House of Representatives election]] he was redistricted to [[Georgia's 120th House of Representatives district|District 120]]. The [[Georgia's 117th House of Representatives district|117th district]] was held by Republican [[Lauren Daniel]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lauren Daniel |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Lauren_Daniel |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=Ballotpedia |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, Gaines helped introduce legislation to create a panel that would give the state more oversight over district attorneys and make it easier for residents to recall prosecutors. Gaines pushed for the legislation following criticism that Athens-Clarke County District Attorney [[Deborah Gonzalez]], who lost her state House seat to Gaines in 2018, was mismanaging her office, saying, “It is past time we take on rogue prosecutors in Georgia who are putting lives in danger every single day.”<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bluestein |first1=Greg |title=Georgia DAs could face new oversight under GOP measures |url=https://www.ajc.com/politics/georgia-das-could-face-new-oversight-under-gop-measure/67NBPFTYQVHX7BCNF5KS5BIFDI/ |publisher=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution}}</ref> In May 2023, Georgia Governor [[Brian Kemp]] signed the bill into law, establishing the Prosecuting Attorneys Qualifications Commission (PAQC).<ref>{{cite web |title=Gov. Kemp Signs Legislation Creating Prosecuting Attorneys Qualifications Commission |url=https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2023-05-05/gov-kemp-signs-legislation-creating-prosecuting-attorneys-qualifications}}</ref>

In 2026, Gaines along with another Republican candidate, Jim Kingston, received over one million dollars in campaign funding by [[Leading the Future]] super PAC backed by [[Andreessen Horowitz]] and [[Palantir]] co-founder [[Joe Lonsdale|Joe Lansdale]]<ref>{{cite web |last=Nichols |first=Hans |date=2026-05-22 |title=OpenAI-linked PAC doubles down in Kentucky |url=https://www.axios.com/2026/05/22/open-ai-pac-kentucky |website=www.axios.com |location= |publisher=[[Axios (website)|Axios]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260523052207/https://www.axios.com/2026/05/22/open-ai-pac-kentucky |archive-date=2026-05-23 |access-date=2026-05-26}}</ref>.
